title: extending `blocking="render"` to allow for a manual control of page holding from the script

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

I have a web page where the whole page is drawn through a canvas using webgpu.
Unfortunately image decoding into a VideoFrame and WebGPU init is async,
which means there is a mandatory flash of a content, even though the init doesn't take long, only maybe a hundred milliseconds.

Another example would be `async import(url)` or a toplevel await with some work, there are a lot of places with async init. As was already requested before: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7976

### What solutions exist today?

One way to solve it would be using a hack with `visibility: hidden` on the root element, unfortunately it degrades very badly, and still doesn't completely solve the issue.

`blocking="render"` was added specifically to replace the above hack: https://github.com/WICG/view-transitions/blob/main/document-render-blocking.md#anti-flicker
unfortunately because of the artificial limitations it is utterly useless for most of the use cases where the anti-flicker hack is used.

`<link rel="expect" href="#the-fold" blocking="render">` doesn't work because:
> If the requisite element is not found, rendering would be unblocked when the document parsing finishes.

One way to hack around `blocking="render"` is to place it on an element with an artificially delayed source.
For example:
`<script src="/delay?delay=1000ms" type="module" async blocking="render"></script>`
and then calling `document.getElementById("delay")?.remove()`
1000ms would be a maximum specified timeout for the render blocking here

This has two big problems:
1. requires to have a service worker (which themselves require an async init) or web server with an useless endpoint.
2. when you call `.remove()` the request isn't cancelled! (at least in chromium) browser still waits for the response, and as I see the only way to cancel it is by using `window.stop()`, or by stopping it from the source (like having a service worker reject the promise)

Another way to hack around it would be to artificially delay the html itself from the server, using a chunked HTTP stream, and use `<link rel="expect">`. Again this isn't any better than the above.

### How would you solve it?

I'm thinking if `<link rel="expect" href="#dynamically-async-inserted-element" blocking="render" some-very-special-attribute-to-allow-unblocking-from-js>` worked or alike, that could be a solution.
I'm not sure about what would be the best way to go around it.

I think the following properties are desirable:
1. be specified in the html as some element, to let the browser know that blocking is expected before parsing the JS
2. allow to set a timeout, could be mandatory

### Anything else?

https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9332 had `document.renderBlockUntil(loadBlockingResources);` as an initial proposal.

_No response_
